newsitem.title: CHINA: Sino-Australian malt venture begins construction.
newsitem.headline: Sino-Australian malt venture begins construction.

text.p: Construction of China's biggest beer ingredient processing plant has begun in the northeastern province of Liaoning, a company spokesman said on Friday.
The Sino-Australian joint venture Dalian COFCO Malt Corp Ltd is expected to process 300,000 tonnes of malt a year when its plant begins full production by the end of 1999, the spokesman said.
The company is a joint venture between China National Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export Corp (COFCO) and Australia's Top Glory Proprietary Ltd.
The venture was forecast to have annual revenues of 1.3 billion yuan ($157 million) and net profits of 130 million yuan.

The first phase of the construction was expected to be completed in 1998 and the plant would have an initial processing capacity of 100,000 tonnes, the spokesman said. He declined to provide further details.
China produced 15.46 million tonnes of beer in 1995, state media has said.
